Reproduced in isolation on the same local Postgres — one connection holding `SELECT id FROM accounts WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE` (account-lock.ts:19-24, which suspension.ts:273 runs first), a second connection inserting a VALID autonomy_suspended row under `SET LOCAL lock_timeout='2000ms'` -> SQLSTATE 55P03 `canceling statement due to lock timeout`. findings.title: The RT-4 fix replaced one false comment with another: the test does NOT discriminate an own-connection helper, and a planted own-connection mutation SURVIVES
findings.arbiter_reasoning: CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT this round, not by re-reading the fix. The owner closed the real gap rather than softening the claim: promised test 29 was added at suspension.integration.test.ts:616, and the old comment at :576-601 was rewritten to state the two things it does NOT discriminate. Re-planting M10 verbatim — `writeRefusalEvent`'s INSERT and its `occurredAtFragment` argument rerouted onto a fresh `postgres(process.env.DATABASE_POOL_URL, { max: 1, idle_timeout: 1 })` — the new case FAILS (baseline: exactly one executed test, exit 0; mutant: exactly one executed test, numFailedTests=1). The survivor is now killed. The kill MECHANISM was verified separately, because the new comment states it as fact and a comment claiming an unmeasured mechanism is the exact defect RT-8 named: the failure duration is 30016ms against the describe block's 30_000ms timeout, so the case dies by TIMEOUT and not through its surviving-row assertion — exactly as the comment says. The lock interaction it names was reproduced in isolation on the same database: connection A holding account-lock.ts's `SELECT id FROM accounts WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE` (which suspension.ts:273 takes first), connection B inserting a valid autonomy_suspended row under `SET LOCAL lock_timeout='2000ms'` -> SQLSTATE 55P03, because migration 116:74's `account_id … REFERENCES accounts(id)` makes that insert need FOR KEY SHARE on the locked row. Both halves of the comment's characterisation are therefore true. The residual note the comment already carries is accurate and unchanged: `ci:db-imports` matches only the `@/lib/db/server` specifier, so a bare `postgres(…)` inside src/lib/refusals/ is caught by no audit — this test is the only thing that catches it.

The SECOND, smaller half is fixed too: the row now scopes its evidence explicitly — 'the default-rule claim is unaudited in **production** (CONFIG-1's evidence is a 2026-06-24 audit of `repworth-nv/repworth-staging`)' — and that citation matches CONFIG-1's own note verbatim at :158-161 in project slug and date. The factual mechanism it rests on re-resolves: AutonomyGovernorScheduler.ts:116 is `Sentry.captureException(error, { tags: { subsystem: 'autonomy_governor' } })` with no level override, versus write.ts:294's `captureMessage` explicitly at `level: 'warning'`.
